queries.query: Othin's own account of hanging nine nights on the wind-swept tree, pierced by a spear and sacrificed to himself, to win the runes
queries.note: 'I ween that I hung', 'offered I was to Othin, myself to myself', 'what root beneath it runs' paraphrased; Othin and the runes kept as reader-honest anchors.

queries.query: how the High One beguiled the giant Suttung's daughter Gunnloth to steal the precious mead of poetry, then left her betrayed and grieving
queries.note: 'Full many a word, my will to get, I spoke in Suttung's hall', 'Gunnloth to grief he left', the ring-oath paraphrased; Suttung and Gunnloth kept as names.

queries.query: how are friendships kept alive, and why do false friendships burn hot then cool
queries.note: The half-loaf friend and the untrodden road to a friend's house; counsel on friendship is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
